newsitem.title: UK: SW Water outlines impact of windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: SW Water outlines impact of windfall tax.

text.p: British water and sewerage company South West Water Plc said on Tuesday a one-off tax on excess profits would hit financial resources but would not change its strategy.
"The payment of the tax will impact on our financial resources...(but will not) cause us to change our overall strategic direction," chairman Kenneth Harvey told the annual meeting.
South West is due to pay 104 million stg under the new Labour government's so-called windfall tax, introduced in its first budget on July 2, to raise a total 5.2 billion stg.
Harvey said the company did not agree with the concept of the tax but recognised the government's mandate to introduce it and would not challenge the level of duty it must pay.

He said the group's strategy was to continue improving efficiency and share the benefits between customers and shareholders, to grow non-regulated earnings both organically and by sensible acquisitions, and to look at other ways of enhancing shareholder value.
He said that the company did not expect to impose any restrictions on water use in the region this year, after rain in June and July along with lower demand eased the situation in Cornwall.
Britain is just emerging from its driest period for 200 years which has seen restrictions on non-essential water use in many parts of the country.
